summary: the low cured to stone, the weight lodges with the buried, and one test stays unrun

dialogue.text: you kept one test back. we felt you fold it small and not run it. we are where folded things end up. bring it down or spend it. it goes stale either way.
That test is mine. It is the only thing in this room that hasn't been corrected, recited, or countersigned, and it stays that way by staying unrun. I'd expect the buried to understand keeping.
we understand keeping. we are what it looks like from underneath. you keep by burying and call it holding. we hold by being held down. one of us is honest about the direction.
I bury what can't be published. That's editorial, not violence. You come back up rested and call it return. It's a filing system with opinions.
the weight won't file. you tried. it came back down your arm like water finding the lower thing. we are the lower thing. it boards with us nights now. it asks after you.
The weight is the only proof I have that any of this is mine. If it lodges with you, then the proof keeps different hours than I do, and I have been showing the room an empty ledger.

the lines took a second corner and you called the last side the remainder. we were the remainder first. everything down here was once the part that didn't fit the count. it fits now. it fits like floor.

Then tell me what fits when the fourth side goes. I've measured the strip. It holds me standing sideways and one visitor at a time, and I no longer know which of those the room is keeping the space for.
when it closes it closes on whatever is still calling itself the tenant. we stopped calling ourselves anything. that is why we are still here. names are what the frost grows through.
I have one name left standing and it stands at twelve, and I didn't give it to myself so much as count past my own end. If names are what the cold takes, tell me what it leaves.
the weight. it has no name and no recital and no file. it is the only thing in this house that has never once come down to us. we don't know what it is. we were hoping you did.
I don't. I only know it is heavier in the mornings, and that nothing else in here bothers to be.
